newsitem.title: USA: FBL Fin'l sells, redeems some securities.
newsitem.headline: FBL Fin'l sells, redeems some securities.

text.p: FBL Financial Group Inc, an insurance company, said Monday it sold and redeemed some securities which will increase earnings on an annual basis.
"We believe these transactions may benefit our shareholders through an increase in after-tax income of as much as $1.7 million per year," said Tom Gibson, FBL chief executive officer, in a statement.
FBL said it sold $100 million of trust securities issued by FBL Financial Group Capital Trust, a newly-created subsidiary business trust of the company.
Simultaneously, FBL said it redeemed $100 million of series A voting preferred stock held by its majority shareholder, the Iowa Farm Bureau Federation.
The securities issued by the Trust consist of $97 million of trust preferred securities acquired by the Iowa Farm Bureau Federation, and $3 million of trust common securities acquired by the company.

The Trust invested the proceeds from these issues in an equal amount of subordinated deferrable interest notes issued by the company. The subordinated notes and trust preferred securities, both of which mature on June 1, 2047, are guaranteed by the company and pay at an annual rate of five percent, payable quarterly.

Concurrent with the redemption of Series A preferred stock, FBL said it sold to the Federation five million voting shares of a new series B preferred stock with a liquidation value of $3 million. The series B preferred stock pays annual dividends of five percent of the liquidation value, payable quarterly.

Except for the maturity of the subordinated notes and trust preferred securities on June 1, 2047, FBL said its cash flow requirements for debt service and dividend payments were not changed by the transactions.

FBL is a holding company for Farm Bureau Life Insurance Co, Western Farm Bureau Life Insurance Co and Utah Farm Bureau Insurance Co. It underwrites, markets and distributes life insurance, annuities, property- casualty insurance and mutual funds in 15 midwestern and western states.
